Instead of asking children who is popular, we can read rank off the game:
PageRank on the network of tokens sent. Code: `code/si/S9_behavioral_rank.R`.

```{r s9-setup}
```

```{r s9-bsr}
```

## How close is it to the nomination-based rank?

```{r s9-correlation}
```

## Tables S53–S54. Cooperation GAP on the behavioral rank gap

Each table estimates how the Cooperation GAP changes with the sender's Behavioral Social Rank minus the receiver's. Column (1) has no fixed effects, column (2) adds classroom fixed effects, and column (3) adds sender fixed effects. Standard errors are in parentheses.

```{r s9-regressions}
```

### Table S53. Observed tokens

These models use the Cooperation GAP calculated from all observed transfers in each sample.

#### All dyads

```{r}
knitr::kable(table_s53[["All dyads"]])
```

#### Mutual friends

```{r}
knitr::kable(table_s53[["Mutual friends"]])
```

#### Non-friends

```{r}
knitr::kable(table_s53[["Non-friends"]])
```

### Table S54. Filtered tokens

These models use the Cooperation GAP for pairs in which both transfers survive the null-model filter.

#### All dyads

```{r}
knitr::kable(table_s54[["All dyads"]])
```

#### Mutual friends

```{r}
knitr::kable(table_s54[["Mutual friends"]])
```

#### Non-friends

```{r}
knitr::kable(table_s54[["Non-friends"]])
```

## Table S55. Asymmetric friendships

These models use filtered tokens for one-sided friendship nominations. Direction is defined by the nominator's Behavioral Social Rank relative to the recipient's. The higher-to-lower group includes equal ranks, following the rule used in the code.

```{r s9-asymmetric}
```

### Lower to higher Behavioral Social Rank

```{r}
knitr::kable(table_s55[["Lower-to-higher"]])
```

### Higher to lower Behavioral Social Rank

```{r}
knitr::kable(table_s55[["Higher-to-lower"]])
```
